sentences.text: Megalneusaurus was a large pliosaurid plesiosaur, a marine reptile characterized by a large head and short neck.
Most recent estimates suggest the animal grew to between 7.6 and 9.2 meters long, though a 2024 study estimated its length at approximately 9.8 meters with a body mass of 12 tons.
It possessed four flippers, with the rear pair larger than the front, suggesting it swam using a method known as subaqueous flight, treating its limbs as hydrofoils.
Wilbur Clinton Knight first described the animal as a species of Cimoliosaurus in 1895 before elevating it to its own genus in 1898, naming the type species Megalneusaurus rex.
The only known species is found mainly in the Redwater Shale Member of the Sundance Formation in Wyoming, United States, within Oxfordian-aged rocks.

A specimen from the Naknek Formation in southern Alaska was referred to the genus in 1994; Wahl and colleagues reclassified this Alaskan fossil as M. rex in 2010, though some authors remain doubtful about its attribution.

Based on stomach contents, Megalneusaurus fed on cephalopods and fish, though it may have also eaten contemporary plesiosaurs. The Alaskan specimen suggests the animal occupied colder waters with less diverse fauna.
Knight concluded in 1898 that the fossils belonged to a pliosaur, comparing them to Pliosaurus and Peloneustes. Cimoliosaurus rex is a synonym for Megalneusaurus rex.
When Megalneusaurus lived, the Sundance Sea where it inhabited was mostly less than 40 meters deep.

Some paleontologists consider the genus dubious due to the loss of most fossils, while others maintain its validity. In 2003, Ellis noted that many researchers doubted the diagnostic value of the holotype due to lost fossils, while others held the opposite opinion.
